title: Council Post: Preserving Authenticity In PR: Bridging Human Touch And AI Innovation
text:
Katie Jewett is a vice president at UPRAISE Marketing + Public Relations, helping B2B tech visionaries amplify their voices.
The fusion of human expertise and AI innovation stands as the cornerstone of effective communication strategies. As we traverse the realms of automation and technological advancements, upholding the authenticity and personal touch that human interaction brings to PR endeavors becomes increasingly crucial. In some cases, this may mean holding back on the temptation to rely on AI, although it does provide an edge in many areas.
This article will explore strategies and best practices that allow us to harness the power of AI while preserving the essence of human interaction, ensuring that PR efforts remain grounded in authenticity and meaningful connections. This includes avoiding an excessive reliance on AI where its default output may fall short.
Preserving Human Touch
Human-led PR has long been synonymous with fostering authentic connections with journalists, built upon the pillars of emotional intelligence and nuanced understanding. Skilled PR professionals adeptly tailor pitches, anticipate journalists’ needs and adapt communication styles to enhance personal connections with the media.
It is this human touch that builds trust and credibility and fosters genuine relationships, paving the way for a more effective and lasting impact in the ever-changing PR landscape. However, as we navigate a fast-paced world driven by automation and AI, it becomes imperative to slow down and connect with the humans behind the computers we seek to reach.
AI Tips For The PR Industry
It’s important to use processes that ensure the same standards are being maintained when AI is used. Here are some initial thoughts on that:
• AI-generated text often fails to take into account important elements like tone, public sentiment and pertinent details. These include each client’s particular needs and expectations.
• Excessive reliance on AI is often easily detectable, as AI text is sometimes hastily cobbled together. This is not only typically a suboptimal result, but also gives the wrong impression to the publisher, the reader and the client.
• As people turn to AI for answers, they must maintain a critical stance. This means continually questioning the veracity of any form of AI-generated output. It could be subject to glitches, errors and all other forms of inaccuracy.
Given these factors, we gain more insights by integrating AI with key trends, storytelling techniques and effective strategies for collaborating with journalists.
Major Trends In The PR Industry
The PR landscape is characterized by several key trends that shape the way we engage with media and stakeholders:
• Erosion Of Trust In Media: Instances of fake news and misinformation have eroded trust in traditional media outlets, necessitating a focus on authenticity and credibility in PR efforts.
• Mounting Business Pressures: Traditional journalism faces challenges with shifting business models, prompting outlets to explore alternative revenue streams like subscriptions and online advertising.
• Competition For Attention: An unprecedented volume of content vies for audience attention, making it essential to craft compelling narratives that resonate amid the noise.
• Shrinking Newsrooms: The closure of numerous news outlets underscores the importance of building meaningful relationships with journalists amid dwindling resources.
Here are some tips for addressing those challenges:
Crafting Compelling Stories
Effective storytelling lies at the heart of successful PR endeavors. Utilizing the acronym “TRUTH,” PR professionals can ensure their narratives are “topical, relevant, unusual, tension-filled and human-centric.” By understanding the dynamic between journalists and PR experts, we can tailor pitches to align with journalists’ interests and audience preferences.
Navigating The Media Landscape
Understanding the nuances of the media landscape empowers PR professionals to tailor their approach effectively. Distinguishing between news categories—from news articles to opinion pieces—helps in crafting pitches tailored to specific outlets and audiences.
Building Relationships With Journalists
Solid relationships with journalists are paramount to PR success. By understanding journalists’ needs, deadlines and preferences, PR professionals can become valued partners rather than mere content providers. Leveraging emotional intelligence and a nuanced understanding of journalists’ interests fosters collaborative partnerships built on mutual respect and trust.
Using Big Data For Better Insights, Faster
AI text generation is often most effective when it draws upon a custom dataset. It can also scrape and analyze large datasets, aggregating online news articles and forum posts to measure consumer and public sentiment, which can provide strategic insights, sometimes with alerts. AI-analyzed data may allow PR agencies to understand more about consumers of a brand so that they can speak to them more effectively. This may be one of the biggest edges AI will offer from a strategic standpoint.
Key Takeaways
To successfully bridge human touch and AI innovation, it’s important to understand the media landscape by staying informed about media consolidation, journalist preferences and emerging trends. When using AI tools, be sure to do so responsibly to enhance PR efforts while upholding ethical standards and compliance.
As you integrate AI into your operations, here are a few things to consider:
• Leverage software integrated with AI to derive invaluable insights and receive alerts by harnessing extensive data accumulation.
• Utilize AI applications for various organizational tasks such as management, internal communication and scheduling, enhancing overall efficiency.
• Employ AI tools to optimize net promoter scores (NPS) for clients. This can be achieved through the implementation of chatbots with instant access to vast databases, offering cost-effective solutions and enhancing customer satisfaction.
Like most technology, it’s also critical to prioritize quality over quantity. Focus on crafting compelling narratives and fostering meaningful connections rather than inundating journalists with irrelevant pitches. While tending to these innovations, don’t forget to build genuine relationships with journalists based on mutual respect, understanding and collaboration. In this way, AI can be used to streamline the creative process by developing templates, researching and brainstorming, rather than as a crutch or a means of churning out content.
Users of AI should also be wary of whether reliance on AI ends up reducing their ability to write and think. This would certainly not be an ideal development in the long term.
The future of PR lies in striking a delicate balance between harnessing AI innovation and preserving the human touch. By embracing technology while prioritizing authenticity and relationship-building, PR professionals can confidently navigate the evolving landscape, ensuring lasting impact and meaningful connections in an increasingly digital world.

Addressing these concerns requires a balanced approach that includes transparent communication about the use and benefits of AI, stringent data privacy measures and reassurance that this adoption is meant to augment human capabilities, not replace them. By emphasizing a human-centric approach, you can mitigate fears and build trust in AI tools as key supports for personal and organizational growth.
A Call To Action For HR Leaders
The integration of AI-based skills frameworks and talent intelligence platforms represents a significant opportunity to lead the way in creating agile, forward-thinking and skills-based organizations. By embracing these technologies, your HR team can accelerate the transformation from the roles of administrative overseers to strategic partners in shaping the future of work.
The call to action is clear: Harness the power of AI so you can develop a workforce that's not only prepared for the challenges of tomorrow but capable of driving innovation and growth. title: Council Post: Security Triad For Leveraging AI
text:
Security Strategist and Vice President of User Experience at Netwrix, visionary and technology evangelist in cyber security space.
Artificial intelligence (AI) has become prevalent in significant business processes. For example, AI already filters potential scam uploads and powers recommendations in many popular apps and services. Its outputs are increasingly important for organizations, and it is often granted privileged access to sensitive and even regulated data.
However, the technology behind AI tools is very different from the familiar IT stack, and it has emerged quite rapidly. As a result, IT and security teams often don’t fully understand its inner workings and dependencies.
All this makes AI an attractive target for threat actors, who recognize that it provides new and powerful avenues for compromising data security. Accordingly, security teams must ask a key question: How can we ensure the security of data accessed or generated by AI-powered tools?
Let’s explore how AI technology can be secured using the CIA triad model: confidentiality, integrity and availability.
AI And Data Confidentiality
Like it or not, some of your organization’s users are almost certainly utilizing third-party AI tools like ChatGPT. While they may be aware of what is appropriate and inappropriate to share on social media, the perceived confidentiality of a “one-to-one chat” with an AI tool can lead to misplaced trust.
Therefore, updating your organization’s security training with AI messaging is crucial today. This training should guide users on maintaining compliance and security while using AI. In particular, educate them about the following best practices:
• Avoid sharing sensitive information with third-party AI tools.
• Anonymize any information shared to prevent identification of yourself or your organization.
• Exercise skepticism about advice from AI, as these tools are not yet capable of real intelligence but are sophisticated data analysis tools.
Even internal AI systems like Microsoft 365 Copilot don’t guarantee data confidentiality. An internally deployed AI model typically has access to private and confidential data, and you must ensure it does not become a back door for a data leak. For example, new documents generated by Copilot do not inherit any sensitivity labels from the source documents. As a result, new documents containing sensitive data could be exposed to unauthorized users. Moreover, Copilot relies on the permissions assigned in Microsoft 365; if users have been granted inappropriate access to content, then sensitive information can quickly spiral out of control.
To address these challenges, look for ways to leverage familiar security controls in the new reality. For example, it is crucial to maintain a least-privilege approach to data access rights. Implementing automated data discovery and classification is vital to ensure accurate and timely labeling of newly generated content so that you can apply proper security controls around it to maintain confidentiality.
AI And Data Integrity
We don’t know how exactly AI models come to specific conclusions. Many times, they are better than average human decisions, but you have probably seen examples of poor judgment and even hilariously wrong responses from AI systems. And since the AI decision-making process is a black box for us, it will be hard to tell when outputs may have been manipulated to an adversary’s advantage.
One strategy for ensuring trust in the integrity of AI systems is to verify their decisions. For example, you can have human auditors examine a sample of AI outputs monthly or after a certain number of transactions. Manual inspection can uncover errors, biases and unexpected outcomes.
A more scalable but more complex approach is overseen by another AI model. That is, a secondary AI scrutinizes the decisions of the primary AI, searching for irregularities, biases and departures from the norm. A dual-layered approach combines human insight with the efficiency of AI, providing a balanced mechanism for monitoring AI applications.
You should also consider more proactive controls, such as filtering and sanitizing both input and output for the AI models. In particular, it’s important to uncover injection attacks (such as SQL injection), in which threat actors hide malicious code within otherwise legitimate input data from a client to the application. Unlike traditional code, in which data and syntax are distinct and therefore easy to identify, AI language models operate within a natural conversation. This absence of definitive syntax makes sanitizing more complex. You have to continuously improve filters to identify potentially malicious input when it comes through a chatbot on your website or an AI tool implemented by the R&D team. A more complex secondary AI approach may also help establish typical input and output patterns and user behavior and then flag or even block deviations from those baselines.
AI And Availability
Finally, you should consider the availability of both AI models and the systems and processes they are enabling. What happens if a system is overloaded by unnecessary or unauthorized requests or even by a maliciously crafted request that chews up the available computing power? How does this impact the rest of the pipeline that the AI is a part of? What impact will it have on your customers and the business?
To avoid availability issues, consider security controls such as comprehensive access management and high-availability deployments, in addition to the input filtering discussed above.
Conclusion
AI industry experts tell us we are still in the early stages of AI evolution. This insight implies that our comprehension of the associated risks and effective mitigation strategies is also in its infancy. However, you can use the CIA triad, your current security expertise and many existing security controls to build a solid foundation for securing AI-powered systems and processes.

title: Council Post: EQ Vs. IQ: Navigating The AI Revolution With Emotional Intelligence

title: Council Post: How AI And Humans Will Transform The Current Education System
text:
MacKenzie Price is the founder of 2hr Learning.
Few things are more important than education. Unfortunately, the U.S. education system has been under siege for years, with understaffed schools, overcrowded classrooms and overworked, underpaid teachers. The government’s own NAEP issued a Nation’s Report Card revealing less than a third of U.S. eighth graders can do grade-level math. I believe we can no longer accept a system that’s failing so many of our students.
The greatest problem stems from the fact we’re still applying a rigid, century-old education model to the challenges of our modern world. Today’s teachers hold the impossible job of educating 20, 30 or even 40 students in a classroom, kids from vastly different backgrounds and aptitudes—with no time to focus on personalized learning.
In this environment, a teacher doesn't have time to give each student the attention they require to excel. As a result, gifted students quickly get bored with the standard curriculum, while struggling students fall further behind, which is often where they’ll remain. Research shows that an underperforming student in third grade is likely to remain an underperforming student when they reach eighth grade because the system isn’t designed to identify exact knowledge gaps and catch kids up.
Years of learning science show one-on-one instruction is highly effective at achieving individual student mastery in academic subjects. Yet that solution is out of reach for most schools.
A New Type Of Classroom
Over the years, school systems and specialized learning institutions have employed different methods aimed at fixing problems with student comprehension, but few have addressed the core issue: the lack of qualified teachers. According to a survey from the National Center for Education Statistics, close to 90% of public school districts struggle to hire qualified teachers and 45% of public schools report feeling understaffed going into the 2023-2024 school year.
Ten years ago, I examined the systemic problems with traditional education and decided we needed a fundamental paradigm shift. We needed to re-imagine education. I opened a private school where students can learn at their own pace through tech-based, personalized systems as an alternative to the lecture-based, crowded classroom approach. My program wouldn’t be possible without the incredible advances in AI that allow learning apps to adapt to each student’s needs and aptitude level.
But technology alone isn’t enough to transform education. I believe that the future of education lies in the synthesis of human expertise and AI tools; combining these two powerful forces will allow us to create accessible, scalable and affordable educational models for all students. Here are some of the key ways educators can use AI to upend the status quo and address students’ individual needs.
Customized Curriculum And Support
At the 2023 Stanford University AI+Education Summit, researchers, students and industry leaders discussed the opportunities and challenges around AI in education. One of the big takeaways from the event was that "great teachers remain the cornerstone of effective learning," but "AI presents an opportunity to support teachers as they refine their craft at scale."
Participants were excited about the potential for AI to help educators quickly update curriculum, assess student aptitudes and adapt lessons to individual students with real-time feedback, plus recommend strategies for bridging knowledge gaps.
Traditional school systems don’t historically succeed at identifying these gaps because their approach isn’t personalized. If a student misses a concept, the class moves on. That student may never achieve full comprehension, which can lead to poor grades, frustration and disengagement or worse—absenteeism and later, the decision to drop out of school.
AI excels at identifying what students know and don’t know. Adaptive, AI-powered apps can pinpoint a student’s academic abilities and knowledge gaps so educators can create a curriculum tailored to their specific needs and intervene before a student sinks into that spiral of frustration.
Cooperative Co-Teaching
AI has infinite time and patience. It doesn't care how long a lesson takes or how many times students ask a question. It will continue to work with students until they've mastered a concept.
These qualities are especially helpful for educators who are managing busy classrooms with learners of different levels and needs. In the traditional model, educators often get bogged down in grading papers and figuring out how to provide customized curriculum, when they really want to work directly with their students. AI is a smart, reliable aide that frees them up to focus on the part of teaching they love.
Creative Solutions
AI excels at delivering creative lessons and learning aids that engage students through their unique interests. For example, when my daughter was studying for her AP art exam, she used AI to create her own study tool—Taylor Swift-style songs with the lyrics adjusted to help her memorize concepts for her exam.
Think about how long it would have taken for a human teacher to do the same thing for a single student, let alone an entire classroom. In contrast, AI can deliver incredibly creative, customized solutions that engage students in ways that were impossible before.
Looking To The Future
While AI can be an excellent teacher’s aide, the human element is crucial in education. For all the good it can do, AI doesn't understand human motivation, empathy or connection.
For example, we had a student come to us as a fourth-grader who was falling behind academically. One of our guides (we call them guides, not teachers) got to know the student and his interests, figuring out he loved football and, specifically, the Denver Broncos. The guide showed him the class leaderboard and asked where he would be if this were an NFL draft. The student concluded that he wouldn't be drafted at all, based on his performance, and that relatable reference to football motivated this disengaged student to take his studies seriously. AI doesn't understand this kind of interaction, so human teachers or guides need to work hand in hand with AI to connect with students on a personal level.
I believe AI will continue to be a game-changer in education. School districts that ban it stand to put their students at a distinct disadvantage. It would be like a school banning student internet use 20 years ago. One of the biggest benefits of using AI in the classroom is that it prepares students for the future, helping them become comfortable with new technologies and develop valuable skills.
If educators can harness AI’s best applications to complement their own methods, knowledge and experience, they can make critical improvements to an ineffective system while providing students with some of the most important tools they’ll need for future success—both in academics and in life.

title: Council Post: Is Your Business Ready For The Conversational Web?
text:
Amit Ben is the Founder and CEO of One AI.
The digital landscape is no longer a museum of static websites. Users have evolved from passive browsers into active participants seeking conversation, engagement and a dynamic online experience. This transformation underscores a move away from the early internet's passive consumption model, where information flowed in one direction, to a more dynamic and participatory sphere.
We are now in the era of AI agents—conversational companions that are redefining how businesses connect with their audience and turning passive browsers into clients, casual visitors into active participants and window shoppers into leads.
A New Norm Of Interaction
Today’s users who visit websites of companies they like and trust expect a quality AI agent to meet them right at the virtual doorstep. While traditional browsing and searching are great, often users are not interested in the time-consuming task of digging through information on their own or navigating through endless menus and FAQs. They want immediate answers delivered through the tool humans use every day: conversation.
Remember the restricted, structured chatbots of yesteryear? The ones that left you muttering to your screen in frustration? Those days are over. Today's AI agents, powered by modern generative models like GPT, are capable of understanding context, detecting nuances in language and delivering responses that are not only accurate but also tailored to the individual user's needs. This level of sophistication has raised the bar for customer engagement, blurring the lines between human and machine interaction.
The shift to conversational AI has revolutionized customer engagement and how we interact with brands online. Users captivated by this convenience often become loyal customers, while others seek it elsewhere. It's not just about the technology; it's about valuing natural communication, time and comfort, which fosters trust. Adopting AI agents can help earn user trust and show care, making each interaction meaningful and keeping your brand trusted in the era of AI.
The Achilles' Heel Of AI Agents: Overcoming Limitations
Conversational AI agents have become a revolutionary force in the digital landscape, seamlessly integrating into business strategies. Yet, beneath the surface of this groundbreaking technology lie inherent challenges that demand attention. Unchecked, these limitations can undermine the very benefits AI agents promise.
These challenges manifest in three key areas: AI hallucinations, off-brand responses and the inability for real-time fact-checking.
AI hallucinations, where the technology fabricates misleading or false information, pose a significant threat to the credibility of customer interactions. Similarly, off-brand responses disrupt the carefully curated brand voice, confuse customers and chip away at the distinct identity a brand has worked hard to establish. Finally, the challenge of integrating real-time fact-checking remains a hurdle. In today's dynamic information landscape, AI's inability to verify information against the latest data risks disseminating outdated or incorrect details—further eroding customer trust.
However, recognizing these limitations isn't a dead end; it's a call to action for businesses seeking advanced AI solutions. The goal is to move beyond these pitfalls and find or develop tools that leverage AI's conversational prowess while ensuring the integrity of interactions. Ideally, these solutions would:
• Provide accurate, real-time information. Customers expect up-to-date responses. The AI should access and utilize the most recent data to deliver reliable answers.
• Maintain consistent brand voice and tone. Brand identity is crucial. The AI should seamlessly align its responses with the brand's established language and style.
• Offer insightful customer interaction analytics. Analyzing user conversations allows businesses to customize experiences and refine engagement strategies, effectively digesting the voice of the customer on a large scale.
• Deliver a user-aware conversational experience. AI should adapt to individual needs while remaining firmly aligned with the brand's ethos. This fosters trust and loyalty by meeting immediate requirements and reinforcing a positive brand image.
By proactively addressing these Achilles' heels, you can ensure that AI agents go beyond mere customer engagement tools. They will become trusted companions, reflecting the best aspects of what brands have to offer. Ultimately, the future of conversational AI hinges on crafting solutions that overcome these limitations. This allows AI agents to not just engage users, but to forge lasting relationships built on trust and brand loyalty.
Leveling The Playing Field For Businesses Of All Sizes
As the AI world is transforming, it’s moving away from the exclusive domain of giants like OpenAI, Google and Bing. The democratization of AI is now making cutting-edge technology available to all businesses, sparking innovation and providing solutions that cater to a variety of needs.
A new wave of companies is emerging, delivering AI solutions that rival or even eclipse those of the industry leaders. Agile and innovative, these firms are creating powerful, business-ready tools to directly tackle common AI pitfalls—like hallucinations and the need for accurate fact-checking—while granting users complete control and transparency. This represents a significant opportunity for smaller businesses to offer competitive, highly customized AI solutions.
Today, AI is all about customization, enabling businesses to implement technology that fits their specific goals and enhances customer interactions. This move toward democratization is not just about wider access to technology but also about enabling businesses to innovate, compete and flourish with AI.
The End Of Clicks, The Dawn Of Conversations
As user expectations continue to evolve, one thing remains clear: AI agents are here to stay. Businesses that recognize the shifting sands of customer engagement and embrace conversational AI as the new norm will be the ones to thrive.
By understanding user needs, addressing the limitations of AI head-on and crafting AI interactions that are both informative and delightful, businesses can shape a future where customer engagement is no longer a one-way street but a captivating conversation.

title: 10 Ways To Get Started In AI (without Being Technical)
text:
It’s easy to feel behind with artificial intelligence. If you haven’t figured out how to integrate tools like ChatGPT into your business, if you don’t know the difference between ML and NLP, or if you feel overwhelmed with all the breaking AI news, you might think you’ve missed the boat. Luckily, that’s not the case. AI is just getting started. Business breakthroughs, huge progress, and a whole new level of efficiency are waiting for professionals just like you to discover today.
Allie K. Miller believes that, “AI isn’t the future, it’s now.” As an AI leader, advisor and investor, Miller has worked with hundreds of companies on AI product development, implementation and deployment. Previously, Miller was Amazon Web Services’ global head of machine learning for startups and venture capital, founding the group and growing it into a multi-billion dollar business line. She was also a lead product manager for AI products at IBM. As the most followed voice in AI business, Miller shares practical resources on building an AI-first company to her 1.5 million followers. For her work in AI business and education, she has also been named AI Summit’s AI Innovator of the Year and LinkedIn’s Top Voice for Technology 2019–2023.
“One of the biggest myths of working in AI is that it’s only for engineers,” said Miller. “That couldn’t be further from the truth.” She added, “AI companies and AI projects need everyone, including marketing specialists, HR leaders, salespeople, operations managers, finance and legal professionals. The tools are more accessible than ever, and this is the opportunity of a lifetime.”
Miller is helping others build a career in the AI age, starting with this list of ten ways to become more familiar with AI technology and the value it offers, ranked from easiest to hardest.
10 ways to build a business and career in AI: start your transition
1. Read AI trends and test tools
“Begin by enriching your knowledge,” advised Miller. “Subscribe to AI-focused newsletters like The Rundown AI or Ben's Bites, and follow leading voices such as former Google chief decision scientist Cassie Kozyrkov, Wharton professor Ethan Mollick, or futurist Sinead Bovell.” Listen to people who have been in the game for a while and turn insights into action by actually testing out tools. Make sure theory leads to practice.
“Start with AI tools like ChatGPT and Perplexity AI,” added Miller. “Make learning AI a habit and stay informed. It will pay dividends when it comes to getting value out of AI.” It’s never too late to begin learning how to apply this technology to your business and career.
Time required: A few hours per week. Cost: $0.
2. Forecast your job’s evolution
Predict the future of your specific role by assessing where you’re at. “Go on LinkedIn or Indeed and look up AI-specific versions of your current role,” advised Miller. “If you’re in sales today, look at sales roles in AI. Then do a gap analysis between the roles you find and your current skills and work to close the gap.”
The next version of your existing role may require proficiency with a handful of tools. “A designer might have to know Adobe Firefly, or an account manager might have to know Salesforce’s AI tools,” added Miller, who recommends you spend a few hours learning those tools, consult YouTube for step-by-step tutorials, and update your resume when you’ve mastered them for real. “Understanding and demoing these tools will give you that significant edge” to clients and employers.
Time required: 10-20 hours. Cost: Tool subscriptions vary.
3. Find an AI mentor
For the next level up, find someone who has successfully made the transition from your current role to an AI-centric one (or several). “This could be an ex-colleague, someone who went to your college, or a stranger on social media,” suggested Miller. Ask their advice on entering the AI space.
Entrepreneurs can find the AI version of their current business by searching online for tools in their space, and get ideas on how their offering could adapt. Either way, make use of other people’s experience to shape your own. “Get concrete, role-specific advice and act on it,” added Miller.
Time required: 10+ hours of search, outreach, scheduling, networking. Cost: $0. Resource: Another person.
4. Attend an AI conference or event
You don’t know what you don’t know. Go deeper in your research by attending a conference and having your eyes opened to new and exciting technological concepts you didn’t realize existed. Meet new people and understand their work. “Conferences can be a huge leg up for networking, meeting hiring managers, and learning where this tech is headed,” explained Miller.
“If you're more technically inclined, attend events like NeurIPS or CVPR. For less technical fields, consider industry-specific events like ScaleUp AI for investing or MAICON for marketing.” Turn up with an open mind, take loads of notes, and follow up with everyone whose work piques your interest.
Time required: 3-5 days. Cost: Conference entrance and travel.
5. Enroll in AI courses
Even though AI is rapidly changing formal education, Miller believes “credentials can open doors.” Don’t just rely on building your own knowledge, find courses tailored to your career goals and “formalize with certificates as required.”
If you’re an aspiring machine learning engineer, “try Python courses from Free Code Camp, ML crash courses from Google and Fast.ai, or Andrew Ng's ML courses,” recommended Miller. If you’re a non-engineer, look into courses like “What is Generative AI?” on LinkedIn Learning, “AI for Everyone” by Andrew Ng, or enroll in Miller’s in-depth “AI for Business Leaders” on Maven.
Time required: 2 weeks to 6 months. Cost: Course price.
6. Implement AI in your company
With the basics covered, you can build up a portfolio and begin creating. “Start meaningfully applying AI in your current role,” recommended Miller. “For example, a data analyst could suggest AI tools for data transformation, or learn a no-code platform to build an ML forecasting model. A customer support manager could lead their team to adopt customer service tools like Zendesk or create a prompt repo for common support needs.” This is AI-ification in action. Apply resourcefulness to find the tools, then monitor the impact (both qualitative and quantitative) on your team’s output.
If you run your own company, empower your team to multiply their output with AI, and figure out solutions together. Prioritize solutions that bring meaningful and positive results, such as freeing up time to work on new ideas that will grow the entire business. “Take initiative and carve out an opportunity for real, hands-on project work,” said Miller, whether you’re building within your role or business.
Time required: Weeks to months. Cost: Enterprise-grade AI tool subscriptions vary. Resource commitment: Team and/or manager alignment.
7. Join a machine learning (ML) side project
If you want to transition into AI but you’re not ready to take the leap in your current business, “engage in an AI collaboration on the side.” Miller suggested you “join Slack or Discord groups, contribute to open-source communities through GitHub, or tap into LinkedIn groups.”
Be deliberate, not haphazard. “Choose projects that resonate with your interests, like sports forecasting models if you’re a basketball fan or botany web apps if you’re a nature lover. I know hundreds of people building AI apps for friends or family,” she added. Pitch your skills and meet new people. You never know what you could co-create.
Time required: Nights and weekends for months. Cost: API usage or tool subscription. Resource required: outside team.
8. Start your own machine learning project
“For the self-motivated, initiating your own AI project can be incredibly rewarding and a great outlet for creativity,” said Miller, who recommended leveraging whatever spare moments you have, emphasizing quality of time over quantity. Learning from the ground up is a great way to understand machine learning, so you can build out your AI-first business or incorporate AI into your role with the fundamentals covered.
“This option is often for engineers,” explained Miller, but “non-technical folks can check out no-code platforms like Builder.ai, Bubble.io, or MindStudio, or bring on a development partner to collaborate and bring ideas to life.” Execution is key, but getting started is the hardest part.
Time required: Nights and weekends for months. Cost: API usage or tool subscription, talent.
9. Work with an AI startup
“Nothing beats hands-on learning, and working at an AI startup is like navigating a jungle on a unicycle. Unpredictable but exhilarating.” said Miller. Collaborating with a startup is a great way to understand the intricacies of working in an AI-driven company.
“Ensure there's no conflict of interest with your current role and do your due diligence to look into the team and investors,” Miller suggested, then roll up your sleeves and don’t hold back. She added that this approach could initially involve reduced rates until you prove yourself and build up your resume.
Time required: Potential for part-time or full-time role.
10. Start an AI company
“This is the most challenging and ambitious path, and it’s one that demands dedication, risk-taking, and resilience,” explained Miller. You need to fully commit for any hope of success. “90% of startups fail, so be sure your motivation is not just financial reward,” she added.
Even if your AI company doesn’t succeed, you’ll have learned a ton and picked up valuable connections. Even “the potential for impact and fulfillment alone can make it worth it,” said Miller. If you think you’ve got what it takes, find a core audience and solve their problem in an AI-driven way. Listen to their feedback and hit product-market fit.
Time required: Full-time and beyond. Cost: Varies widely (thousands to millions of dollars) depending on product and team.
How to get started in AI: from an expert in artificial intelligence
“AI roles are some of the fastest growing on LinkedIn,” explained Miller, who describes these ten options above as not one-size-fits-all solutions, but “stepping stones to a more AI-first career.” If every business will one day be an AI-first company, you can future-proof yours by getting a head start.
Whichever step you pursue requires curiosity, passion and determination. “Your ability to learn, engage, adapt, and practice is going to come down to your initiative. So take the first step now to build a stronger career in the AI age,” added Miller. Put the work in now, and you’ll be forever grateful that you got ahead.

title: Council Post: How AI Can Improve Outcomes In Clinical Home Care
text:
CEO of Rialtes, a global business consulting and cloud-based property management solution company headquartered in Austin, TX.
Artificial intelligence (AI) is disrupting nearly every major industry, and healthcare is poised to become one of the most impacted fields. In fact, according to a Binariks report, the global market size for AI in healthcare is projected to reach $173.55 billion in 2029—over ten times its market size in 2022.
The rise of AI in healthcare coincides with increased efforts to focus on home care. From predicting medical events to sourcing cheaper alternatives to brand-name medications, the past few years have uncovered countless use cases for AI in home healthcare.
For home healthcare, AI’s analytical capabilities could help caregivers and providers respond faster to patients in need and even accelerate diagnostic processes. In some cases, the quick access to real-time data AI provides could mean the difference between life and death for a patient. In many other cases, AI could play a pivotal role in empowering patients to improve their well-being and enjoy more independence, particularly in aging populations.
Let’s explore some of the most important ways AI is shaping clinical home healthcare today.
AI In Optimizing Care Plans
The aftermath of a serious injury or diagnosis typically involves a long, complex plan for recovery. Such plans often involve around-the-clock monitoring, frequent doctor visits and meticulous home care instructions.
AI can make complex home care plans much easier to manage for patients, providers and caregivers. Generative AI can analyze critical patient data across disparate sources, from clinician summaries to medical records, and create ultra-personalized care recommendations. This instant analysis can save providers and caregivers hours of work every time a care plan is updated or adjusted based on new data.
Additionally, these plans can be tailored to patients’ habits and lifestyles, improving adherence to care plans.
Intelligent Health Monitoring
As innovations like the Internet of Things (IoT) and real-time data analytics are woven into the clinical home care space, the healthcare industry is seeing an uptick in intelligent monitoring systems. Using sensors, wearable devices and smart apps to gather data on patients’ vitals and movements, intelligent monitoring technologies can alert authorized caregivers to abnormalities that could indicate a medical emergency.
But apps and wearables only scratch the surface of AI’s potential in health monitoring. For instance, Stanford Medicine is partnering with On Lok, a senior healthcare organization, to improve care for elderly patients using intelligent technologies. In this joint research project, motion-detecting sensors and computer systems were placed strategically throughout elderly participants’ homes to monitor 17 clinically relevant activities. The goal of this project is to enable seniors to enjoy independence and improve their quality of life.
Automated Care Scheduling
When multiple parties become involved in a patient’s healthcare journey, scheduling in-office appointments, caretaker visits and virtual check-ins can become burdensome. Automated scheduling tools can make this process much simpler.
AI can streamline care management by automatically making doctor’s appointments and coordinating caregiver activities. Machine learning (ML) can enable scheduling systems to adapt to factors like evolving patient needs, changing appointment frequency, caregiver availability and more.
With several AI scheduling systems on the market, healthcare organizations can already explore many options that can allow them to take advantage of this emerging technology.
AI-Powered Healthcare Assistants
For patients without access to around-the-clock medical care, AI assistants can now cover some of the duties of an in-home nurse. Virtual nursing assistants are AI-powered tools—usually in the form of an app, chatbot or digital interface—that perform tasks that don’t require the expertise of a medical professional. For example, a patient with type 2 diabetes could ask a virtual nursing assistant common questions about blood sugar, physical symptoms, medications and more.
AI healthcare solutions can also monitor cardiac patient progress remotely to better provide a certain degree of continuous care. These innovations not only provide an added layer of security for patients but also help providers minimize costs associated with home care over time.
Conclusion
As AI’s footprint expands in the clinical home care space, it’s important to fully understand the risks and benefits of incorporating such a powerful technology in a field where clinical precision and data security are paramount.
Despite its promising use cases, AI is still an imperfect technology that, in many cases, should not operate independently of expert supervision. But by prioritizing the safe and responsible use of AI technologies in home care settings, providers can elevate their patients’ care experiences.
The future of healthcare technology is bright. As AI matures, the industry will likely see revolutionary advancements in the way home care is delivered and, as a result, much better patient outcomes.
